extracted.intended_audience: registered patent practitioners (attorneys/agents), USPTO Office of Enrollment and Discipline staff, and others subject to USPTO disciplinary processes
extracted.subtask_description: Standards and procedures for imposing reciprocal exclusion from practice before the USPTO under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24 based on state disbarment, including service, notice, publication, required practitioner duties, and administrative actions (e.g., dissociation of customer numbers).

rubrics_metrics.name: Reciprocal discipline under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the USPTO may impose reciprocal discipline identical to discipline imposed by a duly constituted authority of a State pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This Final Order imposes exclusion because Respondent was disbarred by the Maryland Court of Appeals; reciprocal discipline is ordered when requirements of § 11.24 are met. Action taken pursuant to 35 U.S.C. § 32 and 37 C.F.R. § 11.24.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ground for USPTO exclusion: violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h)
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion may be predicated upon being disbarred from the practice of law by a duly constituted authority of a State, which constitutes a violation of 37 C.F.R. § 11.804(h).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Notice of Exclusion states the practitioner was disbarred and thus violated § 11.804(h); the Director can exclude the practitioner from patent, trademark and other non-patent practice before the USPTO.

rubrics_metrics.name: Service of Notice and Order (certified mail to addresses on file)
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO attempts to serve the Notice and Order by certified first-class mail to the address(es) the practitioner provided to the OED Director.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If service by certified mail to listed addresses is attempted (receipt numbers recorded) but undeliverable, the Office proceeds to alternative service methods as provided in the regulations (see publication).

rubrics_metrics.name: Service by publication when mail undeliverable (37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: If mailed notice cannot be delivered, the practitioner may be served by publication of a notice in the Official Gazette for two consecutive weeks pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.35(b).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Publication notifies the practitioner that copies of the Notice and Order, the Complaint, and underlying state order may be obtained by written request to the USPTO General Counsel; in this case the Respondent was served by publication on May 17 and May 24, 2016.

rubrics_metrics.name: Opportunity to respond within forty (40) days (37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: The Notice and Order must provide the practitioner an opportunity to file, within forty (40) days, a response opposing imposition of reciprocal discipline identical to the state discipline, based on reasons provided in 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The practitioner may assert one or more defenses enumerated in § 11.24(d)(1); failure to file a timely response permits the Director to determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under § 11.24(d).

rubrics_metrics.name: Effect of failure to respond: no genuine issue and imposition of discipline
rubrics_metrics.description: If the practitioner fails to file a response to the Notice and Order, the Director may determine there is no genuine issue of material fact under 37 C.F.R. § 11.24(d) and impose reciprocal discipline (e.g., exclusion).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In this matter Respondent did not file a response and exclusion was determined to be the appropriate discipline.

rubrics_metrics.name: Content of Official Gazette notice of exclusion
rubrics_metrics.description: The Official Gazette notice must identify the practitioner (name, city, registration number), state the basis for exclusion (violation of § 11.804(h) predicated on state disbarment), cite the state order, and summarize grounds for the state discipline (rules violated and factual bases).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The example notice published: identifies Tamara Renee Good, Registration Number 59,644; states reciprocal disciplinary order and violated Maryland Rules; and summarizes factual findings (six separate client complaints and list of misconduct).

rubrics_metrics.name: Types of conduct supporting state disbarment (examples)
rubrics_metrics.description: Conduct found by the state court that supported disbarment included failures in representation, client communication, safekeeping, fees, and cooperation with disciplinary authorities.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically noted were: failed to provide competent representation; failed to pursue clients' objectives; failed to file required documents in ongoing court cases; failed to act with reasonable diligence; failed to respond to clients' inquiries about case status; failed to return unearned fees; failed to provide safekeeping of client property; failed to protect clients' interests when terminating representation; and failed to respond to a disciplinary authority.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duty to give notice of public discipline to state agencies and courts (37 C.F.R. § 11.59)
rubrics_metrics.description: The OED Director must give notice pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.59 of the public discipline and the reasons for the discipline to disciplinary enforcement agencies in the state(s) where the practitioner is admitted, to courts where the practitioner is known to be admitted, and to the public.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This ensures state agencies and relevant courts are informed of the USPTO action.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duties of excluded practitioner under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner is required to comply with the duties enumerated in 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: While the Final Order does not recite § 11.58's text, it directs the Respondent to comply with the enumerated duties (e.g., withdrawal notifications, client communications, disposition of client files/funds per that regulation).

rubrics_metrics.name: Dissociation of USPTO Customer Numbers and PKI certificate
rubrics_metrics.description: The USPTO will dissociate the excluded practitioner's name from any Customer Numbers and the public key infrastructure (PKI) certificate associated with those Customer Numbers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This administrative action severs the practitioner's access and association with USPTO electronic filing credentials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Prohibition on obtaining or being added to a USPTO Customer Number until reinstated
rubrics_metrics.description: An excluded practitioner shall not apply for a USPTO Customer Number, shall not obtain a USPTO Customer Number, nor have her name added to a USPTO Customer Number, unless and until she is reinstated to practice before the USPTO.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This prevents the practitioner from circumventing exclusion by acquiring new or shared access.

rubrics_metrics.name: Public posting of disciplinary decisions (OED FOIA Reading Room)
rubrics_metrics.description: Disciplinary decisions involving practitioners are posted for public reading at the Office of Enrollment and Discipline's FOIA Reading Room.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order cites the URL where such decisions are posted (http://e-foia.uspto.gov/Foia/OEDReadingRoom.jsp) so the public and stakeholders can access the decision.

rubrics_metrics.name: Effective date of exclusion is the date of the Final Order
rubrics_metrics.description: Exclusion from practice before the USPTO (patent, trademark and other non-patent law) is effective the date of the Final Order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Order states the exclusion is effective as of the date of this Final Order and sets forth immediate administrative consequences.
